title: Hiding in plain sight: Adversarial identity concealment for facial gender recognition in edge computing
content:
by Yanxin Yao, Shengdi Zhao, Zhengwei Ni

With the development of the edge computing, privacy protection problems face new challenges due to the end-to-edge distributed computation on different devices of different owners. In order to protect privacy with high efficiency, we propose an idea of transmitting only the information related to main tasks to remote offloading devices, and keeping the private information on the user device itself or nearby safe devices. This paper proposes a distributed layout privacy protection strategy to ensure the bidirectional tasks of gender recognition and privacy protection. The key is to design a favorable feature extraction module with privacy concealment, which runs on user device or nearby safe device through adversarial fine-tuning. And other modules like attribute feature analysis and inference module and attribute classification module, run on other servers. Two effective privacy protected gender identification methods of the local and global fine-tuning method are proposed. The local fine-tuning method freezes either of the feature extraction module or the inference modules, while global fine-tuning method adjusts the weights of all the modules simultaneously. Experimental results show although the local fine-tuning method is more accurate and effective, the convergence speed of the global fine-tuning method is faster and the training process is more concise.
